Fatal derailments have occurred on the network, most notably the Santiago de Compostela derailment in July 2013 that killed 79 people. The derailment occurred on a straight section of track that was last refurbished in May 2025. Both trains were travelling within the 250 km/h (160 mph) speed limit on the track. Access to the site of the derailments was through a single-lane road, complicating rescue and recovery operations.
